audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers contradict each other on the defining interaction. content.mid and whys[4] correctly say Olaf can still be Withered through Ragnarok because Wither is a slow, not hard CC. full.tldr says "His true damage + R ignore your Wither" and full.breakdown.cooldowns says "CC-immune — your Wither won't hold him. Bait it."
audit.why: Ragnarok grants immunity to disables. A slow is not a disable, so Wither applies normally through it — that is the single most important piece of tech in this lane and the reason Nasus is a respectable Olaf answer at all. The full layer tells the player to bait out a 100/90/80s ultimate before using their W, which throws away the whole matchup. The tldr line is also incoherent on its own terms: true damage is a damage type and has no interaction with Wither whatsoever.
audit.corrected: Wither lands through Ragnarok. Use it on the R-engage rather than saving it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Undertow is described as an axe that slows, with no mention that picking it back up resets the cooldown.
audit.why: Undertow is a flat 9s cooldown at every rank, but Riot's text says 'If Olaf picks up the axe, the ability's cooldown is reset.' That means the real cooldown is however long it takes him to walk to the axe — there is no 9-second punish window if the player fights standing on top of it. The actionable instruction is to make him walk back for it, which Wither's move-speed slow makes expensive.
audit.corrected: State the reset and tell the player never to fight on top of a thrown axe.

audit.whatIsWrong: Reckless Swing's health cost is never mentioned, in five separate strings that discuss it.
audit.why: Reckless Swing costs 0 mana but deals true damage to Olaf himself as well as the target, refunding the health only if it kills. In an extended fight against a Nasus with Soul Eater lifesteal and Fury of the Sands bonus HP, Olaf is paying health for every cast that does not finish the kill. That reframes the long trade the content currently presents as pure loss. It also cuts the other way — his passive Berserker Rage scales attack speed and lifesteal off missing health — but the player should know the cost exists.
audit.corrected: Note that Reckless Swing costs him health and only refunds on a kill.

audit.whatIsWrong: Reckless Swing's 325 range is never given.
audit.why: 325 is shorter than his own auto-attack range, so he has to be right on top of Nasus to use it. That is precisely why Wither's move-speed component, not just the attack-speed component, is the answer — it keeps him outside the range of his own best ability.
audit.corrected: Give the range and tie it to Wither's move-speed slow.

edits.before: His true damage + R ignore your Wither — deny axes, build armor, out-scale. Nasus wins by trading around Olaf's Ragnarok and cashing the pattern: deny axes, build armor, out-scale.
edits.after: Wither lands through Ragnarok — it is a slow, not a disable. Nasus wins by trading around Olaf's Ragnarok and cashing the pattern: deny axes, Wither the R, out-scale.

edits.before: Deny axes, build armor, out-scale. Track Ragnarok before every commit and keep the wave on your side.
edits.after: Deny axes, Wither the R, out-scale. Track Ragnarok before every commit and keep the wave on your side.

edits.before: - Olaf Ragnarok: matchup-defining — CC-immune — your Wither won’t hold him. Bait it. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Olaf Ragnarok: matchup-defining — 100/90/80s disable immunity, but Wither is a slow and still lands. Use it.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 belong to Olaf and you just survive them. His Undertow axe slows you and Reckless Swing deals true damage that ignores your durability, so any extended trade he forces before you have Wither is a loss — last-hit with Q at range and lean on Soul Eater lifesteal to soak the poke. Do not walk up to contest a wave he can axe-and-swing onto you. The lane changes the instant you hit level 3 and get Wither: point his attack-speed slow onto him and his Reckless Swing chain and axe-pickup chase fall apart.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 belong to Olaf and you just survive them. His Undertow axe slows you and Reckless Swing deals true damage that ignores your durability, so any extended trade before Wither is a loss — last-hit with Q at range and soak the poke with Soul Eater lifesteal. Undertow is a flat 9s cooldown, but retrieving the axe resets it instantly, so never fight standing on a thrown axe — make him walk back for it. At 3 Wither lands and his swing chain and axe-pickup chase fall apart.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a stack-and-stabilize stretch — Wither lets you peel any greedy all-in, but a fed Olaf still out-trades you raw with true damage, so keep farming Q and don't duel him at even HP. At 6 it evens out hard: Fury of the Sands plus Wither is your answer to his Ragnarok engage. When he pops R to become CC-immune he can still be Withered (it's a slow, not a stun), so slap his attack speed, let your bonus HP and lifesteal eat his swings, and grind the fight back. Bait his R-engage, survive the true-damage window, then turn once Ragnarok ends.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a stack-and-stabilize stretch — Wither peels any greedy all-in, but a fed Olaf still out-trades you raw with true damage, so keep farming Q and don't duel him at even HP. Remember Reckless Swing costs him health on every cast and only refunds it on a kill, so in a long fight he is paying to hit you. At 6 it evens out hard: Fury of the Sands plus Wither answers his Ragnarok engage, and he can still be Withered through R since it's a slow, not a disable. Bait the R-engage, survive it, then turn once Ragnarok ends.

edits.before: Wither comes online — your first real answer, slowing his move and attack speed so he can't stack Reckless Swing autos or chase you off the wave.
edits.after: Wither comes online — your first real answer: Reckless Swing only reaches 325, so slowing his move speed keeps him off you entirely.

edits.before: All-in with Ragnarok active so he's CC-immune through your Wither and his true damage ignores your fat HP bar
edits.after: All-in with Ragnarok up so no hard CC stops him, and let Reckless Swing's true damage ignore your HP bar

notes: The packet's suspectName flag on spikes[0].text ("Reckless Swing's") is a false positive — the ability is named correctly, the possessive just tripped the matcher. The real problem in this matchup was the full layer contradicting the content layer on whether Wither works through Ragnarok; the content layer had it right. Also note full.enemyWin reads "Olaf wins by landing Ragnarok" — Ragnarok is a self-buff, nothing is landed. That is template boilerplate rather than a matchup error so I left it, but the same phrasing will be wrong on every self-buff ultimate in the set.
